### The emergence audit's carriers of the 10 L0 survivors, after T-184's fixes (T-182, T-184) (2026-11-04)

- **What.** T-184: `tools/emergence_audit.py` records NumPy in its cache's `_meta` and refuses a mismatch (the sweep's
  `check_numpy`); `tools/merge_cache.py` refuses a merge while an audit, not only a sweep, runs here; `--criteria`
  runs one machine's share of the rows, `--candidates` one row's share of its carriers, and a share flushes the
  cache without pruning and writes no record; `--render-only` runs nothing. The 15 committed results, unstamped,
  were stamped NumPy 1.26.4 once by hand, as the sweep's cache was on 2026-10-23 (both Macs measured at 1.26.4).
  A new stage `carriers` runs L0 on every in-scope row and the controls and the carriers of each L0 survivor, with
  no L1–L4 (the owner's choice of 2026-11-04); the config is set to it. No file under `src/bowen/` or
  `config/bowen/` changed; the engine hash did not move (`0b363cb3186c`, Phase D `020160abb6db`).
- **The run.** Plan §7 step 6: 113 joint mutants, split across both Macs, 15:19 to 17:19 (Mac Mini1
  `M11.C.48[phase_d]`'s C1–C4 and `M11.C.15` at 10 workers; this Mac the rest at 8 under `nice -n 15`). Both shares
  exited 0; the merge added Mac Mini1's 12 results and found 15 equal; no worker was left on either Mac.
- **Result.** Nine survivors have at least one carrier; `M11.C.48[phase_d]` has none among its seven candidates,
  though its `M11.5` note says it comes from `CUTOFF`'s learned value. Each row's carriers against its `M11.5` note,
  and one proposed T-item per survivor, are in the T-182 record; the owner orders the triage.
- **Tests.** `test_m111g_ea12_carriers_stage_runs_l0_and_carriers_and_no_l1_to_l4` and seven `test_t184_…` tests in
  `tests/test_emergence_audit.py`, each proved red by its mutation (fourteen mutations);
  `test_m111g_ea12_the_config_is_parsed_strictly` takes the new stage. 1335 tests: 1333 pass, 2 strict xfail.
- **Reviews.** learning-qa and a correctness pass on the diff, no high-confidence defect. Fixed: the running check's
  pattern matched the test files' names (now the name must start a word or follow a slash); `--render-only` raised a
  bare `KeyError` on a missing result (now a message, and no record written); a share's L0 gate, `--render-only` and
  the argument refusals had no test. Left: a refused share still rewrites the cache file unchanged, with its NumPy
  version; `--probe` takes precedence over the other options.
- **Documents.** `docs/emergence_audit_record.md` and its cache, `config/audit/emergence_audit.md`,
  `docs/two_mac_sweep.md` (*The emergence audit*), the plan's status line, the T-182 and T-184 record (T-184 ticked),
  `TODO.md`, `docs/TODO_archive.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/theory/_STATUS.md`, `docs/model_explainer.md`,
  `docs/REVIEWER_READING_LIST.md`, `docs/SPEC_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`; `docs/CHANGELOG_archive.md` (stage 3 step 9's
  entry moved there verbatim, for the size limit); `docs/spec_index.jsonl` and
  `docs/spec_coverage.md` regenerated for the new tests; step 4's suite size added to `tests/doc_claims.json`'s
  history.

### The emergence audit, built, and its pilot; spec revision 48 adds `M11.1g` (T-182) (2026-11-03)

- **What.** `docs/plan_v3_emergence_audit.md` §7 steps 1–3: `tools/emergence_audit.py`, `config/audit/emergence_audit.md`
  and `tests/test_emergence_audit.py` (EA-1 to EA-15; EA-16 is `tests/test_doc_checklist.py`). Spec revision 48 adds
  `M11.1g`; the plan called it `M11.1f`, which already held the missing-move rule. Wording only: the engine hash stays
  `0b363cb3186c` (Phase D `020160abb6db`).
- **Proved.** Each test was turned red by the mutation plan §6 names, in a copy of the tree: all 16 red (EA-2 by
  `apply`'s SystemExit; EA-13 and EA-15 by a KeyError in the fixture build, since the changed key or the premise row
  finds no cached result; EA-6 used `witness_window` 13 → 12).
- **The pilot** (this Mac, `nice -n 15`, 8 workers, 28 min): both controls hold (`M11.C.39` red under L0 with
  identical arms, `M11.C.3` survives), and L0's `M11.C.39` row agrees with `learning-off-in-both-arms`. All three pilot
  rows **survive L0**: `M11.C.27[unstable,remove_one]`, `M11.C.41[light: lower level]` and `M11.C.48[phase_d]`
  (`negative_run` +0.245 ± 0.076 with learning off, at 200 seeds, T-180). `M11.C.48[phase_d]` alone took about 23.5
  min, about 17,700 seed-ticks a minute against the plan's 19,000. Carriers were not run (the full stage).
- **Review fixes** (learning-qa and one correctness pass, before push; the record re-rendered from the cache, nothing
  rerun). A mixed row with no premise limbs declared in `premise_limbs()` (`M11.C.41`, `M11.C.34`, `M11.C.11`, pending
  the owner) now says in its note that it is judged on every limb. A Phase C mixed row with premise limbs is refused up
  front, because the Phase C child prints no `p`. An equivalence limb without `within_bound` raises. A control that
  failed to run is reported as not run rather than blamed on the ablation, and the positive control needs a real FAIL.
  A carrier needs a FAIL: a RAISED or UNDETERMINED row is listed but not named. The agreement check raises if plan §2's
  two L0 twins drift, and its disagreement path is tested. Config tables raise on a wrong cell count or a duplicate
  row. Not changed: the Holm family for a mixed row includes the premise limbs, as the runner's does (now stated in
  the docstring).
- **Documents.** The spec, `docs/spec_revision_log.md`, `docs/spec_index.jsonl`, `docs/spec_rules/`,
  `docs/model_explainer.md` §18.6 and §19.6, `docs/SPEC_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/REVIEWER_READING_LIST.md` §5 and
  §7, the plan's status line, `docs/theory/_STATUS.md`, T-180 and T-182.

### Spec revision 47: `M11.C.48` reads both arms under one contact condition (T-179, with T-177) (2026-11-03)

- **What.** The plan `docs/plan_t179_negative_run_contact_condition.md`, built. `first_cutoff_runs` tests contact with
  one function on both sides (`in_contact`, a contact in the cutoff's week or before); a first cutoff on a tie not in
  contact is left out of both arms and counted (`FirstCutoff.contact`, `no_contact`, the report-only
  `no_contact_cutoffs`). Each first cutoff is matched, unmatched or no-contact, and only one of them. The report-only
  `matched_seed` (learning-qa, before the regeneration) gives the share of seeds the arms read. `tools/group_g_readout.py`
  counts no-contact cutoffs in their own column, and `tools/t176_negative_run_trace.py` reads the new criterion first and
  keeps revision 46's readout as a labelled row. T-177's sentence follows the `hold_gain` note in
  `config/bowen/constants.md`.
- **Tests first.** Five new tests and two extended, each red before the change and red under its own mutant (eight
  mutants by hand). A correctness pass found no bug; learning-qa found two (seeds read at 0 against 0 not counted; group
  G merging unmatched and no-contact counts), both fixed before the regeneration. A narrow review of the documents after
  it found four wording and attribution faults, fixed.
- **The regeneration.** The engine hash moved from `09ca2b46c7e0` to `0b363cb3186c` (Phase D `3e03e66ade9f` to
  `020160abb6db`). Mac Mini1 (10 workers) regenerated Phase D part I, part II and the Phase D mutation record (22:45 to
  01:51); this Mac (`nice -n 15`, 8 workers) the Phase C records, level occupancy, group G's "after" section, the
  200-seed trace and the seed-7 trace and export (22:45 to 23:52). Both exited 0; the copied records' hashes are the
  current ones (`docs/version_2_revision_47_changes.md`).
- **Results.** `M11.C.48` fails with no difference (its interval contains zero), no longer the reversal;
  `M11.C.48[phase_d]` passes. Both equal the trace's same-condition row (T179.6). The named mutant
  `cutoff-blind-to-learned-value` survives on `M11.C.48[phase_d]` (T179.7): the pass is not shown to come from the
  learned value (T-180). No other verdict moved.
- **The owner's decisions** (2026-11-03, through `AskUserQuestion`): sweep only `M11.C.48`'s two keys on the new
  engine, into the cache (`tools/version_2_sweep.py --criteria`, this Mac, 8 workers); the sweep record is stale until
  the full sweep reruns (T-181), its test a strict expected failure, and `docs/version_2_status.md` shows W4 unmet on 14
  rows until then. `M11.C.48` stays an accepted finding, its reason restated; `M11.C.48[phase_d]`'s PASS is recorded as
  reviewed, with W1 and W3 unmet on it.
- **Suite.** 1300 tests: 1297 pass and 3 are strict expected failures (`M5.B.3`; `M5.D.3`, T-158; the sweep record,
  T-181). Measured 2026-11-03 on this Mac with `python3 -m pytest tests/`; 52 `ensemble`-marked tests deselected.

### T-179: the owner's decision on `M11.C.48`'s readout, and the plan (2026-11-02)

- **What.** The owner chose option (a) through `AskUserQuestion`: `M11.C.48`'s readout leaves out a first cutoff on a
  tie with no contact by the cutoff's week, the condition the baseline's uncut ties already have, and counts it
  (`no_contact_cutoffs`, reported as `unmatched_cutoffs` is). Options (b), counting uncut ties with no contact at a run

  puts the regeneration across both Macs (about 4 hours) and carries T-177 in the same batch. The owner approved it as
  written the same day, §5's Q1 as recommended (the status page stays live); nothing is built. No rule, readout or record changed, and the engine hash (`09ca2b46c7e0`) did not move.
- **Documents.** The plan (new), `docs/SPEC_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/REVIEWER_READING_LIST.md`, T-179's record,
  `TODO.md` and this file's index (regenerated). The spec, the explainer and `docs/readouts_phase_c.md` are unchanged:
  they describe the readout as built, which has not changed.

### T-176: why `M11.C.48`'s direction is reversed, a trace (2026-11-02)

- **What.** `tools/t176_negative_run_trace.py` runs `M11.C.48`'s 200 seeds on both families as the criterion runs
  them (this Mac, `nice -n 15`, 8 workers, 19 min), reproduces the record's `negative_run` (−0.319 ± 0.104 and
  −0.113 ± 0.062) and sets the cut tie's run against other baselines (`docs/review/t176_negative_run_trace.md`). The
  readout counts an uncut tie only if it had a contact by the cutoff's week but counts a cut tie with none at a run of 0;
  with the same condition on both arms the difference is +0.029 ± 0.136 (Phase B family) and +0.344 ± 0.078
  (twelve-person family). Matching the uncut ties on relation does not remove the reversal. On cut ties with a
  contact, the twelve-person family's run lengthens more than the uncut ties' over 13 and 52 weeks; the Phase B
  family's does not differ. The review passes found the run-before rows carried the same bias; they were
  restricted to cut ties with a contact and the trace rerun once (20 min). The owner restated both
  disposition rows through `AskUserQuestion` and opened T-179 (whether the readout should read both arms alike). Read
  only: no rule, readout or record changed, and the engine hash (`09ca2b46c7e0`) did not move.
- **Documents.** `docs/review/t176_negative_run_trace.md` (new, generated; its "Reading" hand-written),
  `docs/version_2_dispositions.md`, `docs/version_2_status.md`, `docs/spec_index.jsonl`, `docs/spec_rules/`,
  `docs/spec_coverage.md` (regenerated), T-176's and T-179's record, `TODO.md`, `docs/TODO_archive.md`,
  `docs/SPEC_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/REVIEWER_READING_LIST.md`, `docs/REVIEW_version_2_outputs.md` (a row for the
  new page, the owner's mark open), `CLAUDE.md` (the suite count); the test `tests/test_t176_negative_run_trace.py`,
  and the page added to `tests/test_version_2_outputs.py`'s framing list; the page listed as not compared in
  `tools/record_changes.py`, so each of the six change pages (`docs/version_2_stage_1_changes.md`,
  `docs/version_2_revision_*_changes.md`, regenerated) gains that one line and nothing else. The suite: 1295 tests,
  1293 pass and 2 strict expected failures.

- **T-128 (D24–D26, Q14).** `config/sweep/sweep.md` gains `## Named ratios` with `tie_wear_to_transfer_ratio` =
